raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to spread myself too thin, but I also do not dare put all 4.1 mu into one crop. Wheat and maize are still my main steady way, because I know this rotation well and I can use the same land back to back. Cotton I will keep on a small piece, about 1.1 mu, mainly because I have grown it many years and it gives me another source of cash if grain price is not good. On the 3 mu under wheat-maize, I will manage it much like last year: wheat sown in early October with two fertilizer splits and 3 irrigations if water cost is not too high, then maize planted right after wheat harvest with as little delay as possible. I have middle school education, so I listen a little to the township advice, but in the end I still judge by field condition. If the wheat color is poor at jointing, I add some more nitrogen. If rain is enough, I save one irrigation for maize, because pumping from the well costs money. With only 2 people in the house and my age at 78, I keep the plan practical and familiar, not fancy.
